'''Ōshikōchi-no-Katabu''' (''ōshikōchi no katabu''; birth year unknown – Year 9 of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|ja|雄略天皇}}, estimated [[465]]) was a late-{{ill|5th-century|ja|5世紀}} {{ill|Kofun-period|ja|古墳時代}} {{ill|gōzoku|ja|豪族}} and one of the '''{{ill|Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|凡河内国造}}'''. His {{ill|kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} was {{ill|Atai|ja|直 (姓)|lt=Atai|lt_ja=直}}.

== Career ==
The {{ill|Ōshikōchi clan|ja|凡河内氏}} were descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone-no-Mikoto|ja|天津彦根命}}, who was born when {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神}} and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊}} performed their {{ill|ukehi|ja|うけい|lt=oath}}, and they successively held the post of '''{{ill|Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|凡河内国造}}'''.

In year 9 of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|ja|雄略天皇}}, in order to seek a {{ill|divine oracle|ja|神託}} for the campaign against {{ill|Silla|ja|新羅}}, the emperor dispatched Katabu and an {{ill|uneme|ja|采女}} (court lady) to make offerings to the Munakata deities (the {{ill|Three Munakata goddesses|ja|宗像三女神}}). But after Katabu had already arrived at the sacred grounds (''kamuniwa'') and was about to perform the {{ill|ritual|ja|神事|lt=Shinto ritual}}, he had relations with the uneme. The emperor judged this an impiety and dispatched {{ill|Naniwa-no-Kishi Hitaka|ja|難波日鷹|lt=Naniwa-no-Kishi Hitaka|lt_ja=難波吉士日鷹}} to kill Katabu, but Katabu had already fled and was not there. Undeterred, the emperor dispatched {{ill|Yuge-no-Muraji Toyoho|ja|弓削豊穂|lt=Yuge-no-Muraji Toyoho|lt_ja=弓削連豊穗}} and circulated the order throughout the provinces, districts, and counties; at last, near the Ōshikōchi clan's home base in Aihara, {{ill|Mishima District, Osaka|ja|三島郡 (大阪府)|lt=Mishima District}} — later Awigō, {{ill|Shimoshima District|ja|嶋下郡}}, {{ill|Settsu Province|ja|摂津国}}, now Ōta in {{ill|Ibaraki, Osaka|ja|茨木市|lt=Ibaraki City}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}} — Katabu was captured and beheaded.<ref>''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'', vol. 14, Emperor Yūryaku year 9, second month, day 1 entry.</ref> This is the earliest documentary record of a {{ill|beheading|ja|斬首刑}}.

The emperor then intended to lead the expedition against Silla himself, but the deity of Munakata Shrine stopped him with "Do not go (''na imashi so'')," and instead he ordered {{ill|Ki-no-Oyumi-no-Sukune|ja|紀小弓|lt=Ki-no-Oyumi-no-Sukune|lt_ja=紀小弓宿禰}}, {{ill|Soga-no-Karako-no-Sukune|ja|蘇我韓子|lt=Soga-no-Karako-no-Sukune|lt_ja=蘇我韓子宿禰}}, {{ill|Ōtomo-no-Katari-no-Muraji|ja|大伴談|lt=Ōtomo-no-Katari-no-Muraji|lt_ja=大伴談連}}, and {{ill|Oka-no-Hi-no-Sukune|ja|小鹿火宿禰}} to lead the campaign against Silla.<ref>''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'', vol. 14, Emperor Yūryaku year 9, third month entry.</ref>
